(Remove the tabbers for Seliel and Jan) by Samurai viper[]

I think it would be logical to remove the tabbers for Seliel and Jan. Not only do they take up valuable space for a tabber, but they also serve no real purpose compared to the other characters. For Seliel, it seems unnecessary to include a tabber for a character who is disguised as a ninja or not, especially when both images show Seliel wearing the same outfit. If the intention is to showcase Seliel as both a civilian and a ninja, then it doesn't make sense to have her in the same attire.

Jan's case shouldn't warrant a tabber since the only distinction is him wearing a crown in a dream. The presence of tabbers for the Dream Chasers and Zoey doesn't automatically necessitate one for Jan. Additionally, it's important to note that we didn't include tabbers for all Crystal Council members in their normal and Crystalized forms, as we only did so for Aspheera and Vangelis.

Seliel

(Allow Images from Legends of Chima for Wyldness related pages) by KataraEmanuar[]

The Wyldness has caused a lot of renewed interest in Chima and at least one place from Chima is directly mentioned by Ras. According to Ninja72 we're not allowed to use those images because they're from Legends of Chima. However, being this strict is a terrible idea. By that logic then Lloyd Garmadon (The LEGO Movie) should be deleted because it's from a separate theme along with all pages related to Lego Dreamzzz Ninjago crossovers and many others shouldn't be allowed. It's highly likely that the Forever Rock will never be showed in Ninjago and the page will have a no image infobox forever. So we should allow high quality images from legends of Chima. Not allowing Chima images because they're not from Ninjago is a meaningless, awful idea that will definitely result in edit-wars. So please reconsider and decide what to do about this.

Support

  1. Litemods
  2. König Skales
  3. Fritz und Spitz
  4. Carslikesninjago
  5. PrimeEmpireNinja
  6. I feel like the Wyldness shown in the Chima finale, the Forever Rock and the characters that appeared in the S5 finale should be the only exception to the rule, as for example, most Chima characters from Curseworld Part II only had their back shown from far away, and it isn't likely that we will get a full shot of the Wyldness or any shot of the forever rock anytime soon. LB07productions (talk) 18:07, 4 February 2024 (UTC)
  7. The NightStalker's after you! 00:53, 5 February 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. SandNinjaGS (talk) 14:55, 3 February 2024 (AEST)
  2. If we only include info shown in Ninjago, that should apply to images too.Ninja72 (talk) 03:56, 3 February 2024 (UTC)
  3. If that does end in edit wars, then we know how to handle it and issue out warnings to users causing it if needs be.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    10:07, 3 February 2024 (UTC)
  4. Samurai viper (talk) 12:03, 3 February 2024 (UTC)
  5. Akita the Formling (talk) 19:45, 3 February 2024 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. Don’t want this wiki to be flooded with Chima info, but if a picture is helpful to complete the wiki I think it should be added as long as it is clearly communicated where it is from. I need more guidelines from that this looks like before I vote support though. Are we fleshing out the Wyldness page with Chima content or just the forever rock? I personally don’t think the character images from chima should be here if they appear in Ninjago. Also we should wait until locations appear/ are mentioned before having images of them. —Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk)
  2. I think images from Legends of Chima could/should be allowed only for infobox images to Wyldess related pages, in order to illustrate them. Fore instance the Forever Rock. We could only add an image to its infobox because we have images of this place even if it doesn't come from Ninjago. But i don't vote support because that's not exactly what this proposals suggests. Proposal to split the Soundtrack page by Brandini N[]

With the inevitability of all the soundtracks eventually being officially released, as well as the fact that that page is already one of the larger and slower running pages on the wiki, I think that we should split each section of the soundtrack page and make sub-pages for each individual season. This would speed up overall traffic for the pages and allow more focus and details on each season's tracks, as well as allowing the SoundCloud players to function better.

Of course, on the main page we should keep generic info about the music, as well as the other things like individual tracks, general trivia, and videos such as the "Musical Journey" videos.

Support

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 21:49, 13 February 2024 (UTC)
  2.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    21:58, 13 February 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

So how do you plan on titling the sub pages? I would assume the most obvious case would be to title them like this: Ninjago Soundtrack/Rise of the Snakes and not Ninjago Soundtrack/Introduced in season one. And also including the season and number, Season 1 in the title would be quite inconvenient.

Edit: Forgot to mention, Dragons Rising should be the sole exception to this, like Ninjago Soundtrack/Season 1 (Dragons Rising). Also @Brandini N, when you mention one of the tracks we should keep on the main page, that being individual tracks, do you mean for example, character's soundtracks?   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    21:58, 13 February 2024 (UTC)

@LuigiMaster41 Branching off of what you said; my original thought was to name the sub-pages by season number, but your idea for naming them by subtitle is better. Using the season number for Dragons Rising would work better instead though, I agree.

As for the individual tracks, that actually might depend. Even though the other individual tracks section has music such as generic tracks and themes used in various seasons for various purposes, they would probably still be officially released under their season debuts. I think that until their respective albums are released, they should still be listed on the main page.

The "Musical Journey" videos should still be on the main page though, as well as other videos like the recent 13th Anniversary video from Ninjago Music or maybe even behind the scenes videos or interviews.

-Brandini N

Ok then, I think I am following along with what you are planning.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    22:01, 14 February 2024 (UTC)
The result of the vote was: Support

(Deal with the Season 2 onward spoilers) by Samurai viper[]

Ever since the Season 2 sets were unveiled, there has been an ongoing issue with spoilers. More than usual, I believe. Despite constant efforts to remove them, users have persistently added spoilers to various pages. For instance, there have been spoilers regarding Ras and Jordana's connections to the Wolf Clan, as well as Cinder's role as the Elemental Master of Smoke. As a result, the pages for Jordana, Ash, and Smoke had to be locked to prevent further spoilers until April.

However, there is something peculiar about this. When it was revealed in a clip that Chima was part of the Wyldness, we were perfectly fine with adding all the new information related to the realm in both pages. So, why are Ras and Jordana's Wolf Clan outfits still considered spoilers? It seems contradictory. And please, don't just say it's because of spoilers. Here's a better question: if just one clip shows Cinder's status as the Master of Smoke, does that mean we can add that information outside of his article since we also did it with the Wyldness? After all, Cinder being the Elemental Master of Smoke is relatively insignificant compared to the revelation of the Wyldness' reigons and listing them in the page. And it was already revealed in an interview that Cinder possessed Smoke two months before "Ras at Shadow Dojo" was uploaded.

So I suggest that for now on, if a Ninjago clip is released with major spoilers, we should refrain from incorporating those spoilers into previously introduced concepts such as the ninja, Ras, etc. However, we can freely add them in relation to the upcoming content before it makes a debut in the show, as the mere existence of the upcoming content's page serves as a spoiler in itself. To put it differently, it is acceptable to mention on the Forest of Spirits' page that it is located in the Wyldness, but not the other way around. Similar to how we handled the Wolf Clan, we mentioned on the Wolf Clan's page that Ras and Jordana are part of the group, but we did not mention it on their respective pages. We also did this when Crystalized was about to come out, I believe.

Support

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 03:31, 29 February 2024 (UTC)
  2. Ninja72 (talk) 12:07, 29 February 2024 (UTC)
  3. König Skales (talk)

Oppose

Neutral

PixX26 (talk) I am agree to do like that in the future but not to change what is already done : all the changes about the wyldness and chima, because the previous informations were actually wrong (the wyldness and chima being 2 separated realms) so we just updated the pages so that the information are now corrects. It's not really like jordana who integrates the wolf clan that is an evolution of the character's story which should not be spoiled. I don't know if you understand what I mean.08:43, 29 February 2024 (UTC)

Comments

NINJAGO not "Ninjago" by legoanimegirl[]

The NINJAGO brand is not called "Ninjago" but the former instead. Imagine if the LEGO page was instead named "Lego". The horror! The LEGO Website since 2011 has used "NINJAGO" on the official website; to refer to the show itself, the location, the city and toyline. So "Ninjago" is wrong and "NINJAGO" is right. You could consider it minor but again, think about my example with "Lego" insted of LEGO. To impliment this idea would be to change every singe page that says "Ninjago" to say "NINJAGO". Whilst it could take a while, this is a team effort from the wiki and I will do my part as this is my proposal- due to the error bothering me and others I've spoken to.

Support

  1. Mei
  2. Carslikesninjago
  3. Gry1010

Oppose

  2. SandNinjaGS (talk) 6:35, 16 April 2024 (AEST)
  3. It is called NINJAGO® if anything. Does this mean we should use ® too? I don’t think so. Ninjago is a name of the realm and the island and it would look really weird as NINJAGO in every sentence. Matt600 (talk) 20:59, 15 April 2024 (UTC)
  4.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    22:18, 15 April 2024 (UTC)

If it was just about the show name and toyline name, why not (in this case the argument of "LEGO" is valid) but in the cases of the locations in the show I am not agree : In the show universe the locations are written like this : "Ninjago", not "NINJAGO". (We can see it in the subtitles) PixX26 23:19 15 April 2024 (UTC)
  6. Ninja72 (talk) 02:53, 16 April 2024 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. Litemods
  2. Fishlover34 (talk) 18:31, 16 April 2024 (UTC)

Comments

legoanimegirl in response to Matt, The toy line uses the ® due to that being copyrighted. So the "Ninjago (sets)" page should be LEGO® NINJAGO® and the show LEGO NINJAGO/LEGO NINJAGO: Dragons Rising. The show and Island NINJAGO without the ® (outside of toys) and this can be found in trailers for seasons on the LEGO YouTube channel (such as the Seabound finale trailer description). So it's not weird, NINJAGO is an abbreviation, NINJA+LEGO, acronyms are capitalized. So it's not weird it's just a fact and you have to get used to it.

Doesn't LEGO recently stylized Ninjago in lowercase, as seen in The Elemental Mechs shorts and Season 2 of Dragons Rising descriptions? This change by LEGO themselves indicates that Ninjago can in fact be written in lowercase. Furthermore, I believe there was an agreement that we would remove "LEGO" from the names of the shows. And if the capitalization of names is a significant concern for you, it's essential to consider that many other shows and services also have capitalized names, such as DisneyNow, AfroCrowd, Samsung Galaxy A8, and LEGO Avatar: The Last Airbender. This is common and does not detract from the quality or appeal of the content. Samurai viper (talk) 23:06, 15 April 2024 (UTC)
I think another way to do it would be to separate Ninjago the island, realm, city, etc. and NINJAGO the franchise created by LEGO. This would mean references to the show name or the theme name should be fully capitalized because this is how LEGO itself treats the branding, as is the case with the name "LEGO" itself. However, when referring to Ninjago in any other context within the show, it should be capitalized as a typical proper noun, as "Ninjago". Also, the examples shown are how the logos are stylized, not the brand name itself being spelt in capitals. Gry1010 (talk) 23:14, 15 April 2024 (UTC)
I am aree with Gry1010. PixX26 23:25 15 April 2024 (UTC)


legoanimegirl I've seen LEGO use NINJAGO capitalized for the city/island in games, descriptions and toys. Plus subtitles aren't accurate, they have a lot of errors a lot of the time. The show and movie are also both capitalized in many scenarios, whether it be trailers, dvds or the marketing material, which is why I believe it should be dealt with. In the past LEGO was inconsistent with the capitalization due to their YouTube channel being experimental and not having strict guidelines, the website however always had it capitalized whether it was the show or toy line. Plus a wikipedia article being incorrect doesn't mean we should be too, especially considering how long this has been going on. The show internally was always capitalized as well if you look at concept art from either WilFilm or Wildbrain.

WilFilm and WildBrain write the shows' names in lowercase on their actual, official sites. So should we start criticizing them for this? Samurai viper (talk) 00:20, 16 April 2024 (UTC)

legoanimegirl Yes, we should. It's not that difficult to turn on caps lock.

I'm pretty sure that would just mean it's acceptable to have the name labeled regardless it's in caps or not. Samurai viper (talk) 22:16, 16 April 2024 (UTC)
legoanimegirl They're not part of The LEGO Group, so of course they'd make an easy error. However other companies have gotten it right like Warner Brothers and Blue Ocean Entertainment have. Is it that hard to see?

(Split the Characters navbox into Ninjago and Ninjago: Dragons Rising) Matt600[]

Approved by Toa Kopaka Nuva.

I propose that we re-divide the characters navbox into Ninjago and DR. We originally did it that way, but after the vote, the Dragons Rising navbox was removed, since at the time the new series didn't have that many characters. However, after the release of Season 2, there are more characters in the DR show and we have navboxes that contain much less information than we would in this one. The characters navbox is currently too long and, above all, very confusing. Since DR is a new series and may have new fans who aren't interested in the previous show (a survey by Netflix), I don't think it's a good idea to overwhelm them with information they don't need. I see no reason why all characters should be in just one navbox. Other wikis do this for new series as well. My suggestion is that characters appearing only in Dragons Rising would only have this new navbox on their page, characters appearing only in Ninjago would have the current navbox, and characters appearing in both series would have both navboxes. I don't think this is a problem as the rolled up navbox doesn't take up any space.

One of the arguments against it could be that we do not plan to do the same with other navboxes. However, the characters are the most important in-universe element of the series, and there are a lot of them, which is not the case with other navboxes. Perhaps this would also apply to the locations, but they are adequately divided into different sections and are clear. In conclusion, I think that such a solution would improve the clarity of navboxes, simplify access for new fans and help shorten the length of the current navbox, if only by a little.

(Decide how we list villains) by Samurai viper[]

Uncertain about the duration of this situation, there is an ongoing matter concerning some of the characters' roles as villains or not, ranging from minor to major issues.

  • When The Island came out, users kept adding the villain category for Ronin. But it gets removed, because it was just some random scheme he pulled to get money and less drastic compared to Shadow of Ronin. And for Kreel, she tried to sell dangerous artifacts, almost killed to Arin and Sora by having their mech explode, and resorting to kidnapping Lobbo for ransom money.
  • Despite the fact that the Pyro Vipers were being controlled, Zachbarbo doesn't view them as villains. However, does Zachbarbo claim that the New Ninja are villains?
    • Speaking of which, Ulysses Trustable and the New Ninja were perceived as villains by some users because they opposed the ninja and had them apprehended. This raises the question of whether it is fair to label them as villains when the ninja themselves broke the law by releasing Aspheera and causing property damage. Additionally, in Skybound, the ninja were falsely accused by Nadakhan, leading to their arrest by the police after being caught by Ronin, despite their pleas of innocence. Therefore, if Trustable and the New Ninja are considered villains, then the Ninjago Police should also be labeled as such. It is worth noting that the Police Commissioner would have pursued the ninja if his jurisdiction extended beyond Ninjago City.
  • Ukraine and Israel will win a war once said Rapton cannot be considered redeemed simply because he claims to still hate the ninja. This does not provide enough evidence that he is returning to his villainous behavior. It only indicates that Rapton still holds animosity towards the ninja, placing him in a neutral position similar to the Skulkin and the Whack Rats. Are Skulkin and Whack Rats are genuinely redeemed or merely neutral with the ninja? You can even see Rapton associating with the other former oppressive Imperians, such as the Claw Hunters and Imperium Guards, as they come together with the Imperium Teen Resistance Force during a meeting led by Percival, who express his intention to collaborate in order to enhance Imperium for the greater good now that Beatrix is gone.
    • Are we gonna label Levo as a villain simply because it has been confirmed that he harbors animosity towards the other realms, believing Imperium to be the supreme realm of all creation? This belief had led to the Kingdom of Imperium being a closed society, with Imperians having limited knowledge of other realms, resulting in them becoming self-absorbed, a sentiment even Ras detests.
      • Furthermore, should we overlook the fact that the Lava-Tides, who entrusted by the First Spinjitzu Master to safeguard an ancient relic capable of saving the world from destruction, callously discarded said relic into a perilous pit due to their disdain for Wyldfyre, one of the ninja? These actions clearly demonstrates that Rapton's animosity towards the ninja pales in comparison to the deep-seated hatred Levo and the Lava-Tides hold towards other realms and Wyldfyre, respectively. Particularly alarming is the fact that it was shown that the Lava-Tides were willing to let the world perish solely to get back at Wyldfyre for trashing their village even after she cleaned it up.
        • Despite capturing and locking up the ninja under false assumptions and planning to sacrifice them to Wojira to protect Ninjago, the Keepers are labeled as villains in The Island because they're portrayed as a villainous faction in the sets, while the Lava-Tides, who were willing to let the world end due to Wyldfyre's pranks, are not considered villains. If the Lava-Tides were portrayed as villains in the sets, would we start listing them as villains because the sets say so?


So I propose one of these two options:

Give the villains category to actual villains, not anti-villains or simply because they spite the ninja or the sets label them as such.

(Include the villain category to those characters or not) by Samurai viper[]

As previously mentioned, there have been ongoing debates surrounding the classification of certain characters as villains or not, whether it be due to animosity, opposition to the ninja, or simply committing selfish acts. Side note: Mere animosity towards others should not automatically qualify someone as a villain unless they exhibit actual hostility. Interactive Map Linking[]

On the wiki, we have a number of interactive maps, with potential for more to be made as the overall canon continues. However, in order to find, use, and edit them, you have to know what you're looking for, seeing as you have to know the names or type in "Map:[Name]" to find them. This makes them largely unused, especially by the general public such as wiki visitors and new editors.

I propose that we have a section under the three map articles in Category:Maps called "Interactive Maps" which will be used similarly to the "Gallery" or "Transcript" sections in episode articles. As an example of text that could be used, we could use "For the interactive version of this map, click here." which would link to the interactive map.

As for the other maps that may not have articles yet, what's stopping us? I'd be willing, and hopefully some of you as well, to make them. All interactive maps use pictures of maps from the show or official source as a base layer.

Overall, the interactive maps have large potential to expand and become more accessible. They don't exist for no reason, and it would be quite simple to make them easier to find for users.

(Remove TBDCanon and add template for Trivia) by Wikifan988[]

I created the {{TBDCanon}} template a while ago but I no longer feel it's particularly helpful so I would like to propose the template is deleted and instead, a new template is created that can simply be placed at the beginning of Trivia sections of articles about media we might consider "unconfirmed canon". The template would say something like this:

  • Due to the nature of canon in the Ninjago franchise, the exact canonical status of this media is undefined and up for interpretation. As stated by Tommy Andreasen: "Consider stories canon. Unless the series at some point contradicts. The series is the deciding canon."[src]

So to clarify, it wouldn't be a top-of-page notice like {{NCanon}}, but more of an in-text notice like {{VagueAge}}. You can find more of my reasoning for all of this here and discussions by others along similar lines in previous votes here and here. Ultimately, removing the template and placing such information in Trivia would allow for the individual reader to decide on the canon's status, which I would argue is most appropriate given how vague and subjective "canon" can be. Consider, for example, how The Realm of Shadows and Mother Earth are confirmed canon by the creators despite the significant timeline errors in each.

A few other notes:

  • Right now, the TBD canon template is on both media pages (e.g. Mask of the Sensei) and character/object/etc. pages (e.g. Genn), but this new "canon notice" template would only be used on media pages.
  • Installments explicitly labeled to as non-canon by the creators are unaffected by this, but installments labeled as non-canon by us because they contain timeline errors would no longer be considered non-canon.
    • I think Fdsadhratdghsfh's phrasing of "considered canon until proven otherwise (so you'll definitely need solid evidence to prove a project is not canon)" is the best way of framing this, with creator statements pretty much being the only "solid evidence" possible.
  • When there is more context on a specific topic, in other words more creator statements on a specific episode/book/whatever (such as Tommy's statement about Master of the 4th Dimension and Decoded), that information can potentially be added as a trivia subpoint to this, of course mentioning any timeline errors that could lead the reader to decide for themselves that the topic is non-canon.
  • I'm not really sure how to handle non-narrative video games like Chen's Return, but at the very least, the redundant "because video games have never been considered canon" seen on pages like this (which was also my doing, sorry everyone) could be changed to something like "because they are primarily non-narrative." But that feels self-evident so again I'm not sure about this one.

Thanks to Fdsadhratdghsfh for bringing this topic to my attention.

Update: now including two options, one like I described above and another for a top-of-page notice like {{NCanon}}.

Option 1 - Trivia notice

I propose to add a tabber for Wolf Mask Warriors and Wolf warriors' infobox to represent their corrupted version in addition to their normal version.

Comments

Don't see a proper reason to include a tabber, particularly given that the corruption was only temporary, as they all go back to normal in the end. Furthermore, the inclusion of character forms such as Wu and Cyrus Borg as Cyborgs, the crystallization of the Crystal Council, or the Anacondrai Cultists turning into Anacondrai, all of which are also temporary yet are part of a major plot point or a story arc, raises questions about the necessity of including a tabber of the Wolf Mask Warriors. Samurai viper (talk) 01:36, 3 August 2024 (UTC)

Aspheera and Vangelis do have a tabber with their crystalized version while it is not the case of the other members of the council so if the members of a same group do not get the same treatment why the wolf warrior should have the same treatment as the Anacondrai Cultists or Wu or Cyrus Borg ? your exemple of the Council of the Crystal King was not the best. About the Anacondrai Cultists in my opinion yes they should have a tabber with their Anacondrai version. PixX26 (talk) 01:25, 3 August 2024 (UTC)

I was listing examples where tabber suggestions were rejected too many times. I was saying that people rejected the Crystal Council having a tabber for their normal and crystalized forms, while it was agreed that the only ones that do have a tabber are Aspheera and Vangelis, you would know that by looking at the previous edits of the articles or the vote archives. . And for the Anacondrai Cultists, like I said, it was rejected way too many times because it was only temporary. And for the wolf warriors, their corruptive appearance only lasted forone episode and seconds within another, so they're clearly having the same treatment as forms that were temporary like the fake Anacondrai and Tech Wu. Samurai viper (talk) 01:36, 3 August 2024 (UTC)
Very well so since the decision to add a tabber to a page is made in individual vote (like it was agreed that Vangelis and Aspheera are only ones that do have a tabber, and the Anacondrai Cultists which it was decided not to give them a tabber), giving a tabber to the Wolf Warrior (in the case this vote is accepted) does not call into question previous decisions. PixX26 (talk)
1) In such situations, there is always something that is brought into question, depending on the users and their perspectives on the matter. 2) Considering the reasons behind not providing a tabber for certain characters in a specific form, it does raises the question of why we should include a tabber for a corrupted form that only appears in the end of the season while the ones I just listed were more impactful shouldn't and was rejected too much. And because of that, a mere suggestion to add a tabber for the Wolf Mask Warriors doesn't really provide a solid explanation for why it's necessary. Samurai viper (talk) 02:43, 3 August 2024 (UTC)

(Creating archives) by Quinton1721[]

This proposal would allow administrators and content moderators to archive pages. These pages include, but are not limited to:

  • Successful, failed, and invalid rights requests
  • Non-mainspace pages that are outdated or no longer in use (e.g., MediaWiki pages for the chat feature when it still existed, some past chat logs, Project:Newsletter, etc)
  • The already-existing archive pages for votes
  • Select files that are significant in some way but might not be in use elsewhere on the wiki (e.g., screenshots of pages in 2012)
  • Respective talk pages for the items listed above, given they have content and reasonably won't be in use

A page is archived by protecting the page to sysop level, adding a notice template to the page which will be made if this proposal passes, and adding the "Archived pages" category.

This proposal would allow for the creation of Project:Archived Pages, which would list miscellaneous archived pages, and Project:Staff, which would host staff bios and tenures.

The purpose of this would be to preserve the heritage of the Ninjago Wiki. I've had this proposal in mind for maybe a year now but I didn't want to implement it without community support.

Support

  1. Support as proposer. Quinton1721 (talk) 07:34, 5 August 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

  1. Fdsadhratdghsfh (talk) August 6, 2024 19:01 (UTC)

Comments Seems like a good idea, but I would like more information, such as: How long will this project take, and how many people will it involve? I feel that this wiki already has enough on their hands. What do the details of Project:Staff look like? Is it simply an archive of all staff bios and when they served? Which revision of their about page (if that's what you mean by bio) would that be?

These aren't the only questions I have, but they're the only ones I can think of right now.Fdsadhratdghsfh (talk) August 6, 2024 19:01 (UTC)

(Ninjago Seasons/Shows Count) by TheFifi1[]

I would like to propose changing the counting of Ninjago seasons and series, as LEGO officially does. So not 2 series, but 3 series. "Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu", "Ninjago" and "Ninjago: Dragons Rising". And changing the counting of seasons 11-15 to seasons 1-4. Why? The official LEGO channel counts seasons and recognizes 3 series in this way, and sells it to television and streaming in the same way. I think we should change this, that our wiki should show what is official, not what the fans came up with. The counting as 11-15 is a fan-made idea and the creators considered it their own mistakes with the marketing of the new series after March of the Oni. I suggest doing this: - Season 1: Secrets of the Forbidden Spinjitzu (Fire and Ice Chapter) - Season 2 (Ligtning and Eart Chapter) - Season 3: The Abyss and The Flood (Island and Water Chapter) (name confirmed by Tommy Andreasen) - Season 4: Crystalized (Golden Power Capter) And I also propose to create an article separately about the chapters, i.e. we have an article about season 2, which contains information about Prime Empire and Master of the Mountain + separate articles only about it.

Thinking about it from the perspective of a first-time wiki viewer, I'd be confused by the change and have a hard time comprehending the merging of what I thought were individual seasons. Even Wikipedia, arguably the first source people look at besides this wiki, refers to these seasons by their current numbers. If we were to go through with this, it would create conflicting information and cause confusion. And some of these season groupings do not make sense. You cannot tell me that Prime Empire and Master of the Mountain are the same season the way both parts of Season 11 are. We also cannot combine The Island and Seabound. They must be strictly separated as two different seasons. The problem comes from Lego and there is an explanation for this : Since some years Lego work by years. They consider one season by year and release usually 20/30 episodes in two times. When the seasons have two part it works : 2019: s11 part 1 & part 2 2022: s15 part 1 & part 2, 2023: DR1 part 1 & part 2, 2024: DR2 part 1 & part 2. But sometimes (2020 & 2021) the seasons are shorter (16 ep) and Lego release 32 episodes (= two seasons of 16 episodes according to our way of counting) in 1 year but because they considered 1 year = 1 season they decided to consider PE and MotM as 1 season. (Section Stub Reforms) by Trainerkn[]

I've always inserted the {{Section stub}} template in empty or incomplete sections on mainspace pages. It can be seen below.

This section is a stub. You can help expand this section by adding some information.


However, while editing, I realized that some of us have different ideas of when and what the template should be used for. The MoS does not mention this template, despite listing several sections that are required on certain types of pages, like "Relationships" on Character pages. If these sections (among other sections like "Trivia" that are implied to be required) are left temporarily blank, should we use the template?

I propose that we do. In fact, I want us all to operate on the same page, so I also propose that we add a line to the "Templates" section of the main Manual of Style page along the lines of "The section stub template may be used under sections and subsections where written information is incomplete OR under required sections and subsections that have been left blank.

It makes sense to follow such guidelines because it not only serves as a reminder for us to finish a section, but it helps avoid confusion from standard viewers that see a section heading but no information listed. It may also serve as a way to recruit viewers who want to become editors and fill in the blanks.

Alternatively, we can create a new template that looks the same but replaces the word "stub" with "blank" instead, for the purpose of accuracy. We'd have to hold a separate vote for that since I want to keep this one focused on the {{Section stub}} template.

TLDR: I propose that the {{Section stub}} template should be used both under incomplete sections and required sections that are blank, and that a MoS note should be added to clearly dicate the usage of the template.

Support

  1. Trainerkn 02:59, 13 September 2024 (UTC)
  2. Superbattleshipyamato (talk) 23:30, September 15 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments
For the record, "Trivia" is NOT a required section as I previously believed. This does not impact the proposal, but please be aware of this when deciding whether or not to add a section stub to a "Trivia" section. Trainerkn 03:02, 13 September 2024 (UTC)

I'm not exactly sure if this vote even needs a proposal, the TLDR note pretty much simplifies what it is you want to add, so I think a proposal for a change like that is unnecessary, unless I'm missing something here.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    14:51, 15 September 2024 (UTC)

The purpose of the vote is to have a written record of an agreement standardizing the usage of section stubs. People use them differently, and there's been disagreement about blank sections and the like. Having a vote to refer to can limit disagreements and potential edit warring. If it was a more minor issue, I wouldn't have made a vote. Hope this makes sense! Trainerkn 14:59, 16 September 2024 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Support

(Remove any remaining unknown Elemental Masters and Powers) by Brandini N[]

With the recent addition of the unknown elemental master from the Source Tournament, it seems we have exhausted all possible contenders for said Tournament, though many pages still list various unknown masters and elements that have not been seen nor can be proven to exist. We are all assuming that there are still more competitors to the Tournament, even though all we have seen is background characters and audience members that share designs. The true nature of the tournament bracket remains a mystery, and I doubt we will get a concise list of all competitors any time soon.

Getting to my point, any unknown and unseen elemental masters from the tournament and listings of unknown powers briefly obtained by certain characters should be removed, since there is simply no evidence to prove they exist. To better explain what should be removed:

  • The 6 remaining masters listed on pages such as Tournament of the Sources and Elemental Masters,
  • Any instances of Unknown powers listed on infoboxes such as Nokt's and Sora's, and so on (save for the Cragling power).
  • Of course, we should still keep the Cragling and his power, the bearded master, the goggled master, and the man in the wheelchair, as they all have distinct designs.
  • However, we should remove the page for the goggled elemental master's power, as it's properties and abilities remain unknown for now and the page in my opinion is not up to standard compared to other elemental powers pages.

Overall, I believe this change would cause less confusion and be more true to the information we already have. Feel free to comment if you still have any questions.

Support

  1. To clarify, this essentially just removes the numbers resulting from inferred elements and elemental masters from things like infoboxes? I always thought that was a bit silly when I saw "6 unknown elements" etc. on pages. Trainerkn 20:04, 1 October 2024 (UTC)

  3.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    21:39, 2 October 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

@Trainerkn yes, essentially. Brandini N 20:14, 1 October 2024 (UTC)

  1. I was very confused when I saw these pages start appearing in the mainspace, most of which I deleted, and one I moved. However, upon closer inspection, I figured out the usage. Despite the overwhelming opposition to this idea (which shouldn't have been executed without a vote to begin with), I still appreciate the format and user-friendly design. HOWEVER: Having a table like this for every season is just too much for an appearances section. While too many of you are getting hung up about the amount of work involved, I'm mostly dissuaded by the sheer volume of a page it could occupy when the lists work just fine. Therefore, I'm voting neutral to express my support for similar decisions in the future, even if this one has a few critical flaws that need to be ironed out.
    Trainerkn 18:50, 9 October 2024 (UTC)

  1. Truly just wanted to see how these would look, sorry for all the confusion and leaving them up. Upon seeing them I agree some characters are in far too many continuous episodes to use them. Sorry again! Kidsocarides
  1. Kidsocarides, next time, please make a vote next time you want to make such a big change to the wiki, everyone should also deserve a say in one's ideas too.

Trainerkn, not trying to change your opinion at all, however, are you aware of the amount of pages we would have to change? TONS. I am open for new ideas, however, when coming up with such, its important to also consider how many hands are needed at deck, and how this can affect reader's view, nor just editors as well. I have seen other wikis use an identical template like this for appearances; however, I just think it is way too late to change our appearances section without the exhuastion from many users. So yes, it is too much to change like, pretty much just over half out of 5,527 pages (which I have just checked to make an approximate count) as of this date. Not to say that it is impossible, but it is evident that a good majority of us, even me, are not up to committing to such an idea like that with where we are right now. As mentioned, it is just too late to make such a big change to the Appearances sections on the many pages we use now, so let's just stick to what works now and what the community is used to in this case, which is the lists.   LuigiMaster41    Talk 🌟    21:00, 9 October 2024 (UTC)

I agree with Luigi Master in my logic but I also agree with Trainerkn. If the old method was not good, I would have said yes to this. However, I agree with Luigi Master not to change this since the old method is fine. S29685781 (talk) 21:20, 9 October 2024 (UTC)

Luigi, your statistics really put this into perspective. Again, it's impractical when we have an already-working method, it's just that I want to support experimentation from users and understand what works and what doesn't. If the vote were to get close, I'd be voting in opposition, but I feel currently neutral on this issue for reasons forementioned. I try not to be swayed by the amount of work that results from proposals, but sometimes, it really can be too much. Recently, I've been in a conflict about the Uthaug and Toke Uthaug Rasmussen pages. Since there are multiple characters that are based off real people, like Bragi Schut or Jay Vincent, it's been assumed by some editors that Uthaug is the tv show counterpart of Toke, even if one's name is after someone else's surname. We have other examples of characters being named after real people, like Tommy and Simon and Koenig. The characters based after real people are always a cameo or a gag character being used for humor. Uthaug is used for comic relief, but none of his jokes are linked to the character his name is based on. (Ninjago (TV series) sections into pages) by Wikifan988[]

In the same way that less extensive versions of List of unused concepts and Physical releases were once sections of the Ninjago (TV series) page, I propose that the Influences, Production/Behind the scenes, and Recurring patterns in the series sections are also made into their own pages.

Originally I created these three sections mostly moving info from Trivia, but the length of the page already and the fact that these sections could be organized better if they weren't limited to being one single bulleted list each makes me think they would be better and more accessible as their own pages at this point. "Production/Behind the scenes" would become Ninjago (TV series)/Production, and "Recurring patterns in the series" would become Ninjago (TV series)/Tropes.

"Influences" could be Ninjago (TV series)/Influences, but I'd go for Influences on the Ninjago franchise similar to this Avatar Wiki page. This is because some of the influences in that section, specifically the ones about the Dark Island Trilogy, are not just about the TV series, and it feels more along the lines of the unused concepts page and Culture of Ninjago (which was also inspired by an Avatar Wiki) to have it as its own separate page rather than a subpage.

Some more specifics but feel free to propose alternative/additional ideas:

  • Influences would be divided into lists by media type: Film, Television, Real-life individuals, and Miscellaneous/Other. The lists on this page would also now include media that episode titles are based on, such as "The Day Ninjago Stood Still"/The Day the Earth Stood Still.
  • Production would mostly be paragraphs rather than bulleted lists, divided by sections such as writing and conceptualization, art/design and animation, and changes in format (episode length, and also info about the GDC/Xentrix Studios switch would be also be added).
  • Tropes would be bulleted lists, some sections being cartoon tropes/recurring gags, common beginnings/openings to episodes or seasons, and similarities between seasons and characters. For the last one, the section now only notes how certain villains and seasons resemble each other but doesn't elaborate on how; having a full page would allow us to list those similarities all in one place.

(Change the Manual of Style rule regarding the "element" Infobox field for characters) by Brandini N[]

Earlier, user Boundforthestory made an interesting point on Nokt's talk page saying that all the Elemental Powers Nokt used in the Tournament of the Sources should not be listed on his Infobox in accordance with a Manual of Style rule with elements. Bound later edited Sora's page and removed all her brief elements, which was soon reverted. However, it turns out that Boundforthestory was in the right for doing this. To quote the manual of style:

"element - If a character is an Elemental Master, their Elemental Power should be listed in this field. This does not include listing all of the Elemental Powers a character has possessed. If the character doesn't have an Elemental Power, please leave this field blank."[3]

However, if we were to truly follow along with this rule, that would mean we would also have to remove Golden Power from each of the Ninja, Fire from Aspheera, Darkness from the Crystal Council members, etc. This feels like a bad thing to go along with since these elements are/were a part of these characters and were often vital to entire story lines.

In short, I propose we change this rule to allow and require all Elemental Powers, current and former, stolen or used in the infobox. If the character only obtained a power through possession or a tool, do not include it. It would in my opinion help reflect more of all the abilities and attributes of various characters.

Include parentheses within pages by Wikifan988[]

I propose overturning this vote because while it does arguably look cleaner, I would argue that omitting parentheses in display titles is potentially more misleading (even if unintentionally so) and confusing in the long run, for both editors and readers, and it does not actually look better, just different. Though this is a recent change, there have been multiple times where it took me a moment to process that a page's display title was different than its actual title, and this is as someone who was familiar with the change. So I imagine it would be more confusing for readers who aren't aware of it, especially since most wikis are not formatted this way and we're used to having page titles match their URLs. Of course, adhering to other wikis' formatting is never the sole reason we should do something, especially since things vary from wiki to wiki, but it's still worth taking into consideration as one factor.

Originally I brought this to Trainerkn's attention because it was a large-scale change enacted without a vote, and making a vote was sort of a way to speed up the process and not have to undo and then redo everything in case a vote would have passed anyway. I was in support of the change for the convenience and appearance, but now a few weeks down the line seeing it in practice more, I'm not sure about it because I feel it prioritizes aesthetics over accessibility and ease of navigation.

Support

  1. Wikifan988 (talk) 15:07, 17 November 2024 (UTC)
  2. PixX26 (talk) 15:25, 17 November 2024 (UTC)
  3. Trainerkn 17:28, 19 November 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. LB07productions (talk) 17:51, 17 November 2024 (UTC)
  2. Per LB07. Quinton1721 (talk) 20:51, 17 November 2024 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. This is one of the first votes in a while that I'm conflicted on (not because I made the vote for Wikifan, but because there are great arguments for each side). LB makes some great points about our streamlined navigation system, while Wikifan speaks to the prioritization of accessibility over aesthetics. Right now, I see myself leaning toward support, surprising myself. I'm not tripped up by the page titles, but I know others are. As a wiki, it's our job to provide as much genuinely helpful information as we can, and including the parenthesis may be slightly annoying to look at but will be beneficial for clarity overall.Trainerkn 18:01, 17 November 2024 (UTC)
  2. I feel this needs to be decided on a case-by-case basis, as some pages will benefit from parenthesis compared to others. Brandini N 21:37, 17 November 2024 (UTC)
  3. Matt600 (talk) 20:02, 18 November 2024 (UTC)

Comments I don't see why they parentheses should be readded, since pages that share similar names to others already have a small section informing readers of similar pages or disambiguation pages. Not using the parentheses also keeps consistency with other pages, such as episode pages who have their page names modified. And when other pages link pages with parentheses, the parentheses is always removed unless the other pages is also linked. The only time that the removed parenthesis would be confusing would be when an editor is source editing and doesn't check similar sounding pages when linking, which is easily avoided. Casual readers would simply copy the url to the page if they want to use it for something, which does have the parentheses, and if they simply look up the page again, they would click the result with that matches with what they are searching, and if they do click the wrong page, we have the "not to be confused with" sentence to help them. LB07productions (talk) 17:51, 17 November 2024 (UTC)

Brandini's comment about deciding on a case-by-case basis gave me an idea for a compromise: we continue to omit parentheses in the display titles, unless they are subpages, in which case the parentheses remain. For example, Ninjago (TV series)/Gifs and The Royal Blacksmiths (episode)/Transcript would keep the (TV series) and (episode) in their display titles, but their parent pages would exclude the parentheses and would simply say "Ninjago" and "The Royal Blacksmiths". One reason for this is because subpages already have the actual name of the page right below the display title (see image), so it feels a bit pointless and contradictory to obscure the subpage's actual name. Wikifan988 (talk) 10:09, 19 November 2024 (UTC)

Oh, and disambiguation pages would be another exception, but that seems to already be the case. Wikifan988 (talk) 10:17, 19 November 2024 (UTC)

On second thought, also considering the (Dragons Rising) in the seasons' page titles as something that may be too significant to remove from the display titles, that is a lot of exceptions and would likely be more confusing/inconsistent than either option. So for that reason I revert to my original proposal to keep parentheses in all display titles to err on the side of clarity. Wikifan988 (talk) 10:57, 19 November 2024 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Support

Proposal for the Formalization of the Organization for Character Set Appearance Templates by Arthurwyne[]

I propose for the establishment of a formal style of organization for how the handling of character set appearance templates should go for future use. After scrolling through the wiki, I noticed that there does not appear to be a formal way of organizing this information if a character has had many different minifigure variations released in sets, (in particular the Ninja).

For example, on the template for Kai's set appearances, they are listed in numerical order, but this results in some discrepancies where suits that were released in later years appear before suits that come before them. (For example the 2016 Destiny suits appear before the 2015 deepstone suits), and another issue is that for sets such as polybags or magazine gifts, they are simply added to the bottom instead of being categorized alongside suits of the same design.

Now the thing is, that while this listing seems fine at a first glance, it is not uniform across all the pages of characters with templates to list their set appearances. For Nya and Jay for example, their appearances are listed with every suit together with the boxed sets first, followed by magazine gifts. (I.e., 70677 Land Bounty (armor); 892063 Nya (armor))

What I propose is for the establishment of a uniform way to categorize these appearances. My personal suggestion would be to arrange them in numerical order in the format of "[Box sets], [Polybags], [Magazine gifts], [books]" in the order of the minifigure design variant and by the chronological year they were released. So for example, for Kai, the list would start with the 2011 trainee and DX suits, then the 2012 ZX, Kendo, and NRG suits, etc.

I feel this might be effective for better organization overall, especially if someone wants to locate all sets in which the minifigures with a particular design can be found. If anyone may suggest a different organizational structure or changes to the one I proposed, I would be open to such ideas as well.

Support

  1. I think this is a good idea. While we divide all the episodes and in-universe appearances into smaller sections, we just have this big section called Sets which is really long, unclear, and confusing. This can help with it. Btw you can support your own vote too. Matt600 (talk) 20:02, 18 November 2024 (UTC)

Uniform Set Appearance Template Part 4 by Arthurwyne[]

Thank you everyone for voting on the previous 3 parts to this proposal, and for your patience with me as we continue to iron out the remaining kinks. So for the final part of this proposal, I would like to address and set a precedent for handling certain 'problematic' sets that do not quite fit the mold under the categories established in the previous parts. In particular, this proposal seeks to address sets that are Ninjago related and were retail sets, but were not released under the Ninjago banner (Dimensions sets, Brickheadz, and 40429 Ninjago World), Minifigure Packs (such as 5003085 Minifigure Pack and 5004076 Minifigure Gift Set), as well as 4002021 The Temple of Celebrations, which was an employee gift that was not available to the public outside of 3rd party websites such as Ebay.

Specifically, I seek to answer if these sets should belong under "Boxed Sets," which in prior proposals I have clarified is intended to represent widely available retail sets that have also been packaged in some form of cardboard, or if they should belong under "Misc sets" because the were either not released under the Ninjago banner or because they were employee gifts.   2. So to summarize the multiple parts of this proposal, from now on, we shall rearrange the set appearance lists of characters with multiple minifigure design variants in the following way:
  • From top to bottom, we shall arrange sets in ascending numerical order by the chronological appearance in which the minifigure design was released. So for example, the Skybound Destiny Gi would be listed before the Honor Gi from the Day of the Departed sets, despite having a proceeding number because the Destiny Gi was released first.
  • The appearances in the sets shall be divided with subheadings to categorize the sets themselves, using the following names: [Boxed sets], [Polybags], [Magazine Gifts],[Books with Minifigures], and [Misc sets]. These categories have been arranged specifically in order of most accessible (boxed sets) to least accessible (books with minifigures technically, though misc is at the end cause its misc)
    • With regards to Gimmick sets (Spinners, Epic Battle Time, Airjitzu Flyers), they would go under boxed sets
    • With regards to Ninjago related sets that are not released under the Ninjago Banner (Dimensions, Brickheadz, Legoland), Juniors and 4+ Sets, and Employee Gifts (Temple of Celebrations), they shall be categorized under Boxed sets.
    • With regards to minifigure packs (Bricktober packs, Target Gift Boxes, Elemental Masters and Oni Battle Packs), they shall be categorized under "Misc Sets"
    • These subheading templates shall also be used for characters whose minifigures appear in more than one set medium (for example the Wolf Mask General who appears in 1 boxed set and 1 magazine gift) Arthurwyne 22:51 PM, 3 December 2024 (UTC)

Streamline the Samurai X Mechs by Wikifan988[]

Currently we have three pages for the Samurai X Mechs: Nya and P.I.X.A.L's first, P.I.X.A.L.'s second, and Nya's second. I assume the first two are merged because in "The Quiet One," P.I.X.A.L. and Nya imply the new Season 8 version used to be Nya's, even though it's an entirely different design. I think it would be best to split these pages again into two and simply note this dialogue in the trivia. Even if it is an updated version of the original mech, P.I.X.A.L.'s version fits the criteria for having its own page if I understand this vote correctly, as it is named and appears in a set and several episodes. Meanwhile, P.I.X.A.L.'s second mech (confirmed to be a separate one) appears in only three episodes and no sets, yet it still has its own page.

Along with this split, I propose that besides the original, we rename the other three to be more streamlined:

(Create preload templates) by Samurai viper[]

In recent months, a trend has emerged regarding the creation of pages, where numerous entries are being made without any content, leaving them blank and forcing other users to either fill in the content or have these pages deleted due to their lack of substance. A closer examination can be seen with the Children of the Wolf: Most of the members' pages were created but left blank for hours, with the notable exception of Asa, whose page was created by another contributor…me. This issue extends to several other articles, including the Spectral Crown, and Roby's father, and one of them was even a duplicate article. No offense, but it is particularly ironic that some of the users who make empty pages are ones who criticize others for minor errors, such as typos or missing categories. What makes this situation even more perplexing is that these users were once known for producing well-crafted pages before they began to leave their contributions devoid of content. For instance, the page for 892411 Wolf Hunter was created with substantial information, while just three minutes later, the same user created 112405 Lloyd vs. Claw General, which was completely blank for two weeks.

It's also worth mentioning the due to the pages not being properly laid out, some sections in Season 2, Part 2 episodes of Dragons Rising were disorganized or remain unfinished for weeks/months, one example being "Truth and Lies." And there's also the Season 3 sets.

On one hand, I would say block them from the privilege of creating pages for a specific time such as three days or a week, similar to how the Villains Wiki blocks a user whenever they create blank pages, but I suppose we should suggest giving them another chance since they are in fact contributing.

Anyway, as a way to prevent disorganized or blanked articles, I propose we add preload templates. Click here for more details -> https://dev.fandom.com/wiki/PreloadTemplates. If the vote is accepted, I need a staff member to create MediaWiki:Custom-PreloadTemplates by adding the content listed below it.

Here's what would be added: 

Infoboxes
                * Character
                * Set
                * Object
                * Location
                * Vehicle
                * Creature
                * Element
                * Episode
                * Book
                * Season
                * Individual
                
Quotes
                * Quote
                * Dialogue


Support

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 00:53, 12 December 2024 (UTC)
  2. Strong support for this. Please see my comment below.Trainerkn 17:50, 12 December 2024 (UTC)
  3. This would definitely make streamlining the process of making new pages better. Brandini N 18:08, 12 December 2024 (UTC)
  4. Arthurwyne (talk) 18:43, 12 December 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

I'll have to do more reading, since we may need different configurations for different types of pages, since it seems SV only added Infobox and Quote info. I'm not sure how detailed we plan to be, but I'm assuming we'll make preloads for every type of page expressed in the MoS? Again, this will take some time and effort, but I'm willing to do my part for the benefit of new and experienced editors alike. Thanks for this spectacular proposal, SV!Trainerkn 17:50, 12 December 2024 (UTC)

Change Nolink template by Wikifan988[]

A few years ago I implemented the {{Nolink}} template as a replacement for {{Cite}} in cases where we know the source but simply don't have access to it (because it's a dead link that wasn't archived, for example). However, at this point I feel the Nolink template is too similar to Cite and instead, Nolink could be a template that's just included in regular cite notes and says "link unavailable", or something like "Museum (link unavailable)" when there's more specific information to be given about the unavailable source. This would keep descriptions cleaner and leave the details to the references section. I got this idea from the Ben 10 Wiki.

To clarify, we would go from this:

Information[link unavailable]

To this:

Information[4]

  1. ↑ https://x.com/otherland71/status/1807971523216789532?s=46&t=peBKUn1k8gxJDJ38zxdSOQ
  2. ↑ https://x.com/otherland71/status/1808053855370072231?s=46&t=peBKUn1k8gxJDJ38zxdSOQ
  3. ↑ Ninjago Wiki:Manual of Style/Characters
  4. ↑ link unavailable

Support

  1. Sounds good, since the cite template engages editors to at least try and find the links, while Nolink doesn't. If this change is enacted, we must clarify it in MoS and/or the templates page, to inform editors that they should add the words "link unavailable" in a reference. Great suggestion! Trainerkn 18:27, 18 December 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

(Decide what to do with the Ultra Combiner Mech) by Samurai viper[]

After seeing the Season 3 interviews, it is evident that we need to address the issue with the Ultra Combiner Mech, as it is identified as a form of Zane rather than a traditional mech, despite its name. Long ago, it was said in a vote that we should refrain from creating vehicle components that can merge into a larger vehicle, similar to the Ultra Sonic Raider and the Ninja Team Combo Vehicle. However, the Ultra Combiner Mech consists of two vehicles along with Zane and Riyu, which complicates matters. This raises concerns that users may argue for dedicated pages for P.I.X.A.L. and Sora's vehicles or question the rationale behind creating a page for the Ultra Combiner Mech, given that it is not a mech in the conventional sense. This was emphasized in multiple interviews and reviews, and in my opinion, this distinction is an exception for its page compared to other vehicles.

So, I suggest we go with one of two choices: either create separate pages for P.I.X.A.L. and Sora's vehicles, and remove the page for the Ultra Combiner Mech, or we make the two vehicles and still maintain the page for the Ultra Combiner Mech, just like how the four dragons came together to form the Ultra Dragon.

Make individual pages for the vehicles of P.I.X.A.L. and Sora, while refraining from making a page for the Ultra Combiner Mech.

Support

Oppose

Neutral

The result of the vote was: Oppose

The way these vehicles will function will variate between forms, and therefore, they all deserve pages unless others have strong arguments for overlapping information.Trainerkn 23:40, 24 December 2024 (UTC)

Add "" to a character/object/ability/etc in the appearance section by Draal[]

This something I always found confusing, especially when I first got here but never had time to properly address this "issue". So in the section "First appearance" and "Latest appearance" of an infobox, this always got me confused because the appearance of the subject is right next to its sets appearance, which might lead people to confusion. So to avoid that, could we put the double apostrophes before and after the subject's first/latest appearance in the show? Draal The Deadly (talk)

Support

  1. Fdsadhratdghsfh (talk) December 27, 2024 17:41 (UTC)
  2. Trainerkn 20:10, 27 December 2024 (UTC)
  3. Since it is already automtically present in episode infoboxes and we add it in the appearances section, and book titles are written in italic. LB07productions (talk) 12:00, 28 December 2024 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. I do not really see what is confusing about the current way.Ninja72 (talk) 11:56, 28 December 2024 (UTC)

Comments

  1. Ninja72, the main issue is that longer titles, such as the one pictured, carry over multiple lines. While the editors of the wiki know what we're looking at, visiting users who come for the odd bit of info for a project or the like may not. We want to clearly mark where each topic begins and ends, which we'd use bullet points for, but it doesn't make sense with the appearance fields.Trainerkn 00:47, 29 December 2024 (UTC)
The result of the vote was: Support


Do Maaray Guards count as antropomorphic eels? by Legor4ik[]

It is confirmed that they are eel-like, so I think that they count. Anthropomorphic eel will become a name for a race of Merlopians (earlier, Maaray Guards could be considered a name for a race, but now it is a name for a group, since Fedulian is not a Maaray Guard) so now Teelk and Fedulian will still count as merlopians, but from different races.

However, I'm not sure if the page for normal Eels should be treated like a page for Snakes or like a page for Frogs.

Support

  1. yes I think the eels merlopians should be listed on the Eels page like frogs, snakes, bears and so on.PixX26 (talk) 16:00, 30 December 2024 (UTC)
